podcast.body: Peter Gabriel famously concluded his set with this song, a tribute to South African activist Steven Biko, who died in police custody in 1977. During the performance, band members would progressively leave the stage until only the audience remained, singing the song. This particular performance was recorded in Toronto on July 4, 2003. "Gabriel started the song and then one by one, everyone leaves the stage until it's just the audience singing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song is about Stephen Biko, a prominent anti-apartheid activist in South Africa who tragically died in police custody. The song serves as a tribute and protest against the injustices of the apartheid regime. "Peter Gabriel's Beacon, about the act of a Stephen Beacon who died in police custody."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
